structured.reason: The description contains one implied negative, in the "Benefits for Your Routine" section: "Trim them to fit your eye shape, then apply and go." This reacts to the reviews' complaints that the lashes are too long ("these were to much... they are crazy long," "Just need to measure them and cut them before you wear them," "The bf says they are too long"). Saying the lashes must be trimmed before wearing implies they don't work as sold, which is the backhanded or defensive framing of a known complaint described in category 3, similar to "once you trim the excess, it fits well." It is a close call, since trimming is an ordinary fit instruction, but it addresses a specific review complaint and so fails the no-negative-statements criterion. The rest of the description is plain positive framing: the lightweight and soft claims, the handmade and cruelty-free features, and the variety all lack caveats, and the "cheap" wording from the feature list was left out.
